title: 1. The Mystery of the Injured Bird
text: Imagine you are sitting in your classroom, and suddenly you hear a loud 'tak' sound. A small bird has hit the ceiling fan and fallen down! It looks scared and hurt. What would you do?

title: 2. Time to Think!
text: If you were that tiny bird, how would you feel? Do you think the bird needs a doctor, or does it just need some time, love, and a little water to feel better?

content.title: Helping the Bird
content.description: An interactive animation showing children gently giving water to the injured bird using a small bowl.

title: The Big Reveal: Animals Have Feelings Too!
text: Just like humans, animals feel pain, hunger, thirst, and love. When the children gave the bird water and let it rest, it felt better and flew away safely. Animals depend on our compassion and care.

content.definition: A feeling of deep sympathy and sorrow for another who is stricken by misfortune, accompanied by a strong desire to help.

content.question: If you see a thirsty dog outside your house on a hot summer day, what is the best thing to do?
options: Chase it away with a stick
Keep a bowl of fresh water outside for it

content.tip: Never touch a stray or injured animal directly without an adult's help. You might accidentally scare or hurt them more, or they might bite out of fear!

title: Reflection: A Friend in Need
text: Think about a time when you were unwell or hurt. Who took care of you? Your parents, right? Animals often don't have anyone to take care of them. How can we become their friends and caretakers?

content.mistake: Believing that animals do not feel pain like humans do.
content.correction: Animals have nervous systems just like humans. They feel pain, fear, and sadness just as much as we do.

title: Connection: Food and Friends
text: Different animals need different types of care and food. Chandu Dhobi cares for his donkey by giving it grass and water, because the donkey helps him carry clothes. We feed grains to birds, milk to cats, and grass to cows. We are all connected in a beautiful web of friendship!

content.title: Mastery Challenge: The Bird Bath Project
content.description: Take an old, shallow clay bowl. Clean it, fill it with fresh water, and keep it on your balcony or terrace. Observe it every day. Keep a diary of which birds come to drink water or bathe in it. You are now an Animal Guardian!
